3.npm_audit: After npm install + npm audit fix (non-breaking): 11 vulnerabilities (2 low, 6 moderate, 3 high). Remaining vulns require Astro 6 upgrade, blocked by astro-cloudinary@1.3.5 peer cap on astro ^5.0.0. Pre-fix count was 24 (2 low, 10 moderate, 12 high).

5.preview_redirect_check: deferred — Vercel preview deployment fails (pre-existing issue: missing PUBLIC_CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME in Vercel preview env; confirmed by checking prior deployment also failed). GitHub CI green. Redirect rules added to vercel.json; build dist structure verified locally.

decisions: Moved CATEGORY_CONFIG from posts.ts to slugs.ts so it can be imported in tests without pulling in astro-cloudinary runtime dependencies.

Added getCategoryPath() as a pure helper in slugs.ts; postToListItem() uses it for hrefs. Route params in [category]/[slug].astro and [category]/index.astro now use the plural path value as the URL segment.
index.astro [category]/index.astro getStaticPaths now uses Object.entries and passes categoryKey as a prop (not category) to avoid confusion between the slug-style key and the plural URL param.

RSS fix: rss.xml.ts was generating singular /article/ and /review/ hrefs; updated to use getCategoryPath() so RSS links match the actual page URLs. The Vercel redirect (/article/:path* → /articles/:path*) would have covered subscribers, but canonical RSS URLs should be correct.

One post (2015-03-12-sxsw-2015-a-look-back.md) has malformed multi-line YAML in its category field, producing a path like 'article - austin - screens - sxsw'. This is a pre-existing content issue; its RSS entry still uses the malformed path (not /article/) so it does not match the redirect rule. Flagged for Rod to fix the frontmatter.
npm audit fix --force was NOT run because it would upgrade to @astrojs/vercel@10.0.8 (Astro 6 adapter) and astro@6.4.6, both breaking changes blocked by astro-cloudinary.
assumptions: The Vercel preview deployment failure is pre-existing (prior deployments also failed with 'failure' state) and not caused by Step 3-5 changes. GitHub CI passes for the same build commands.
trailingSlash semantics: vercel.json redirects use ':path*' which matches with or without trailing slash. The destinations don't add extra slashes beyond what was in the source.
